# Parley v0.1.36

Fixes a regression in v0.1.35 that broke panes. Install this build and do not
use v0.1.35.

## Panes no longer go black when you open another one

In v0.1.35, opening a pane blacked out every pane already on screen. Only the
newest one kept drawing. A single pane on its own was fine, so the fault only
appeared once a second pane joined it.

The cause was a change made in v0.1.35 itself. Parley keeps one terminal surface
per pane and hands that same surface to whatever part of the window is showing
it. v0.1.35 started wrapping the surface in a container so that a pane which had
briefly failed to attach could recover on its own. But a view has one parent, and
when the window re-arranges — which is exactly what opening a pane does — the new
container took the surface while the old one was still holding a reference to it.
The old container then hid that surface and pulled it out of the container that
had just taken it.

The surface is handed over directly again, as in every release before v0.1.35.

The recovery that change was meant to add is gone with it rather than rebuilt in
a hurry. A pane whose surface is briefly unavailable shows its message until the
pane is restarted, which is how every earlier release behaved.

## Everything else from v0.1.35 stands

The rest of that release is unaffected and still applies:

- A failed write to the handoff journal can no longer damage the file in a way
  that stops coordination from starting on the next launch. This is still the
  reason to be on a build newer than v0.1.34.
- A timed-out command can no longer hold a thread indefinitely when its process
  cannot be killed.
- A delivery into a pane that is being closed refuses rather than reporting a
  submission that never arrived.
- A backward step in the system clock no longer freezes the window mid-delivery.

## On how this shipped

Neither the automated checks nor the Ghostty soak could see this fault. The soak
exercises the terminal registry directly and never builds the window around it,
so it passed against the broken build, and it passes now for the same reason.
The change had been recorded as having no automated coverage before it was
merged, and it was merged anyway.

The engineering guide now describes the exact mechanism, so the recovery feature
cannot be reattempted the same way.

## Compatibility

Agent protocol is unchanged at 32. Nothing about panes, workspaces or stored
state changed between v0.1.35 and this build, so upgrading needs no cleanup.

Validated: 335 native checks, 53 Node tests, public scan, platform scan, build
and the 25-round eight-pane Ghostty soak. The strongest evidence is not any of
those: the reverted file is byte-for-byte the one that shipped in v0.1.34 and
every release before it, so this build's pane mounting is the behaviour those
releases had. The fault was found by using v0.1.35, and confirming the fix means
opening several panes in this build — the check no suite here can perform.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
